As of **November 17, 2026**, the United Nations is actively responding to compounding humanitarian emergencies, health outbreaks, and regional political transitions across multiple fronts.

---

### 1. Middle East: Winter Rains Compound the Humanitarian Crisis in Gaza

The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) and the World Food Programme (WFP) reported that severe winter weather is heavily impacting displaced populations across Gaza:

* **Shelter and Sanitation Collapse:** Heavy seasonal rains have flooded makeshift tent camps, collapsing embankments and destroying scarce remaining food supplies. Humanitarian agencies note that accidental tent fires—caused by families attempting to cook or stay warm inside restricted quarters—have resulted in fatal child casualties.
* **Severe Food Insecurity:** With over 1.7 million Gazans displaced and 1.4 million facing acute hunger, WFP rations have been forced to stretch further, dropping from one hot meal per day to one hot meal every two days.
* **Access Barriers:** UN humanitarian officials continue to urge member states to press for the opening of additional crossing points to allow weather-resistant shelter materials and essential equipment to enter.

### 2. Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC): WHO Warning on Escalating Ebola Outbreak

The World Health Organization (WHO) convened its Emergency Committee as the Bundibugyo virus disease epidemic in the DRC more than doubled over a three-month period:

* **Scale of Impact:** Over 11,000 cases and 5,400 deaths have been recorded across 67 health zones in eight provinces. Children bear a disproportionate burden, accounting for a third of all deaths.
* **Cross-Border Spillovers:** Limited international spread has been confirmed, with nine cases (and two deaths) reported in Kenya and an imported case detected in Nigeria. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus criticized blanket travel restrictions by external nations, warning that they impede the regional response.

### 3. Afghanistan: Emergency Winter Funding Approved

To mitigate impending seasonal starvation and displacement shocks, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) announced the approval of **$18 million in emergency funding**. The package is targeted at supporting over 824,000 vulnerable individuals through the harsh winter and lean lean-season period.

### 4. Security Council & Global Governance Updates

* **Syria Transition Briefing:** The UN Security Council held its monthly political and humanitarian briefing reviewing Syria's ongoing transition process as the region approaches the two-year milestone following the fall of the Bashar al-Assad regime.
* **Secretary-General Succession Process:** Deliberations and informal straw polls continue at UN Headquarters in New York regarding the upcoming selection process for the next UN Secretary-General, featuring prominent candidates such as IAEA Chief Rafael Grossi and UNCTAD head Rebeca Grynspan.

---
Here is a detailed breakdown of the operational, logistical, and strategic mechanisms behind the UN’s current humanitarian response in Gaza and the World Health Organization’s (WHO) containment protocols for the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Part 1: Gaza Humanitarian Operations — Logistics, Funding, and Access Constraints

The United Nations Humanitarian Country Team (HCT)—comprising OCHA, the World Food Programme (WFP), the International Organization for Migration (IOM), and partner NGOs—is managing a compounding winter emergency under severe structural constraints.

1. Logistical Bottlenecks and Supply Chain Delays

Pre-Positioned Backlog: Humanitarian agencies have staged more than 150,000 winterized tents outside Gaza awaiting clearance. However, incoming shipments face multi-layered approval protocols, narrow delivery windows, and restricted crossing capacities.

Arbitrary Entry Denials: UN officials note that essential shelter items are routinely blocked without formal "dual-use" security designations or technical explanations. Alongside durable tents, critical winterization kits—including generators, fuel, spare parts, water-pumping equipment, and debris-removal machinery—remain heavily restricted.
On-the-Ground Mitigation: Inside the enclave, where Israeli military control covers nearly 70% of the territory and coastal fishing is prohibited, humanitarian teams have resorted to makeshift engineering. Agencies are manually digging drainage channels, reinforcing camp pathways, and filling empty flour sacks with sand to build flood barriers around tent settlements.
2. Funding Shortfalls and Rationing Impacts

Donor Stalling: UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher reported that international funding has fallen significantly short of operational requirements, noting that several donor governments have delayed financial commitments pending political transitions and post-election government formation in Israel.

Food & Livelihood Collapse: Because unemployment exceeds 80% (with 252,000 jobs lost and $2.77 billion in labor income wiped out), over 1.7 million displaced people rely almost entirely on external aid. Due to supply and funding deficits, WFP has halved hot meal distributions in displacement camps from once daily to once every 48 hours, while wet conditions have made scavenging rubbish for cooking fuel nearly impossible.
Operational DimensionCurrent Bottleneck / DeficitHumanitarian ImpactShelter & Winterization>150,000 tents stalled outside borders; multi-step inspection delaysFlooded camps, sandbank collapses, and fatal tent fires from indoor cookingFood SecurityFunding shortfalls and restricted crossing points1.4M in acute hunger; WFP hot meals cut by 50% (1 meal per 2 days)Infrastructure & RecoveryBans on pumps, generators, and heavy debris-clearing equipmentStanding floodwater, heightened waterborne disease risk, and 85.1% unemployment
Part 2: DRC Ebola Outbreak — WHO Response Strategy and Cross-Border Protocols
Following the declaration of a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) for the Bundibugyo ebolavirus (the DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak, centered in Ituri Province), WHO, Africa CDC, WFP, and the UN peacekeeping mission (MONUSCO) are executing a multi-pillar containment strategy.
1. Core Clinical and Epidemiological Strategy
Countermeasure R&D Acceleration: Unlike Zaire ebolavirus, there are currently no licensed vaccines or approved therapeutics specifically targeting the Bundibugyo strain. WHO and international partners are fast-tracking clinical trial readiness—establishing cold-chain infrastructure, training staff in Good Clinical Practice, and expanding local laboratory diagnostics to evaluate candidate vaccines and investigational treatments.
Decentralized Care & IPC: To reduce mortality and prevent treatment centers from exceeding capacity (which previously spiked above 130% in neighboring provinces), WHO is deploying modular isolation units and specialized treatment centers directly inside outbreak epicenters like Bunia, Rwampara, and Mongbwalu. Strict Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) protocols—including systematic facility mapping, triage segregation, and airlifted Tyvek PPE shipments—are prioritized to curb healthcare-associated infections.
Contact Tracing & Community-Led Surveillance: Rapid response cells focus on investigating unexplained community deaths and febrile clusters, aiming to maintain daily contact follow-up rates above the 95% threshold needed to break transmission chains. Because security instability and misinformation hinder access, WHO embeds religious, women, and youth leaders into surveillance, safe-and-dignified burial teams, and survivor clinics.
2. Cross-Border Containment Protocols
Regional Coordination & Point-of-Entry Screening: Drawing on Uganda’s successful containment of an earlier spillover (which ended in July 2026 after 20 cases), WHO enforces joint cross-border protocols across eastern and central Africa. These include synchronized alert notification systems, joint simulation exercises, and millions of health screenings at formal border crossings.
Opposition to Blanket Travel Bans: While countries such as the United States have implemented targeted entry prohibitions and channeled travelers from affected regions through designated screening airports (such as IAD, ATL, and JFK), WHO formally advises against broad international travel and trade restrictions. WHO epidemiologists warn that border closures do not stop transmission; instead, they drive cross-border movement onto unmonitored, informal pathways while disrupting the airlift of medical personnel and supplies.
---
Here is a structured analysis of the three vectors—spanning biomedical R&D architectures, international humanitarian law (IHL) governance, and civil-military peacekeeping logistics—governing the UN's active operations in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Gaza.

Vector 1: Virological Divergence & Medical Countermeasure Pipelines (Bundibugyo vs. Zaire Ebolavirus)

The 2026 DRC outbreak represents a severe structural vulnerability in global filovirus preparedness: the biological and regulatory mismatch between stockpiled tools optimized for Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) and the emergent Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV).

1. Genomic Divergence and Diagnostic Bottlenecks

Genetic Distance: BDBV diverges by more than 30% at the genomic level from Zaire ebolavirus. Consequently, standard RT-qPCR molecular assays calibrated for EBOV (such as standard Ebola Xpert cartridges) initially generated false negatives during the early phase of the 2026 emergency.

Multi-Tiered Diagnostic Architecture: To overcome target mismatch, the DRC’s Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) and WHO instituted a four-stage diagnostic cascade: (1) broad pan-filovirus RT-PCR screening, (2) Sanger sequencing for species-level amplicon assignment, (3) agnostic metagenomic sequencing for divergent isolates, and (4) species-specific qRT-PCR confirmation.
2. Clinical Trial Frameworks & Funding Mechanisms

The Tumaini Adaptive Platform Trial: Launched in Bunia, Ituri Province on October 23, 2026 (NCT07842107), Tumaini ("hope" in Swahili) is a pivotal Phase 2/3 ring-vaccination trial embedding clinical R&D directly into active outbreak response. Rather than relying on static single-arm testing, the protocol uses an adaptive platform design overseen by an independent data monitoring committee to add promising candidates or drop ineffective ones in real time.

Cross-Protection vs. Species-Specific Candidates: Because no licensed BDBV vaccine exists, Tumaini evaluates whether existing stockpiled EBOV vaccines (Ervebo, rVSV-ZEBOV) confer cross-reactive clinical protection alongside newly fast-tracked monovalent BDBV candidates—including Moderna’s mRNA candidate (Phase 1 launched August 2026) and Oxford’s ChAdOx1 BDBV viral vector vaccine (Phase 1 launched October 2026 in Uganda). Simultaneously, the EBO-BOOST-BRIDGE study (led by ITM Antwerp and INRB) is analyzing 600+ banked serum samples to establish serological correlates of cross-protection.
Financing Architecture: The R&D pipeline is underwritten by the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) Bundibugyo development program, backed by pooled sovereign and philanthropic commitments from the European Commission, the U.S. Department of State, and the Fund for Science and Technology, with trial readouts targeted for early 2027.
Technical DimensionZaire ebolavirus (EBOV) BaselineBundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) Status (Nov 2026)DiagnosticsStandardized rapid molecular assays (GeneXpert)Requires pan-filovirus RT-PCR + metagenomic sequencing due to >30% genomic divergenceLicensed VaccinesApproved & stockpiled (Ervebo; Zabdeno/Mvabea)None licensed; Phase 2/3 Tumaini ring-vaccination trial testing Ervebo + 2 BDBV candidatesTherapeuticsApproved monoclonal antibodies (Inmazeb, Ebanga)None licensed; in vitro susceptibility shown for small-molecule antivirals (e.g., Remdesivir); two investigational treatments entering trials in Bunia
Vector 2: International Humanitarian Law (IHL) & "Dual-Use" Governance in Gaza
The stalling of more than 150,000 winterized tents, water pumps, generators, and debris-clearing machinery at Gaza’s crossings sits at the intersection of binding treaty obligations under International Humanitarian Law and unilateral export/import security regimes.
1. Governing Legal Architecture
Affirmative Duty to Ensure Supplies (GC IV, Art. 55): Under Article 55 of the Fourth Geneva Convention, an Occupying Power bears an affirmative legal duty, to the fullest extent of its available means, to ensure the food and medical supplies of the civilian population and to bring in necessary articles if local resources are inadequate.
Obligation to Facilitate Relief Schemes (GC IV, Art. 59 & AP I, Art. 70): Where a population is inadequately supplied, the controlling party is legally obligated to agree to and facilitate rapid, unimpeded passage of impartial humanitarian relief. Under Customary IHL (ICRC Rule 55), parties retain a right to prescribe technical arrangements—such as cargo inspections and convoy routing—to verify that consignments are strictly humanitarian, provided such controls are proportionate and do not arbitrarily nullify relief delivery.
2. Regulatory Friction: Export-Control Frameworks vs. Humanitarian Mandates
Expansion of "Dual-Use" Classifications: Historically, "dual-use" controls derived from multilateral non-proliferation regimes (such as the Wassenaar Arrangement) governing items with both civilian and conventional military/WMD applications. Over the past two decades—and acutely in Gaza—unilateral national security lists have expanded the classification to encompass Critical Humanitarian Items (CHIs), including tent poles, solar panels, water desalination parts, heavy excavators, and explosive-ordnance disposal gear.
Procedural Opacity & Cross-Border Synchronization: Humanitarian legal analyses (including Gisha’s 2026 assessment and Physicians for Human Rights) highlight two systemic breakdowns:
Lack of Standardized Criteria: UN OCHA and NGOs face shifting, opaque vetting lists without published technical thresholds or formal appeal mechanisms, resulting in arbitrary rejections of identical shipments across different inspection cycles.
Regional Spillover: Because inspection clearances at adjacent crossings (such as the Salah al-Din corridor) are closely coordinated with Israeli security authorities, items barred at primary crossings are similarly blocked along secondary routes, eliminating alternative logistics corridors.
Vector 3: Civil-Military Peacekeeping Logistics in Conflict-Affected Ituri Province
Operating an epidemic response in Ituri Province—where active armed militias overlap with 1.7 million people facing crisis-level food insecurity—requires integrating WHO’s epidemiological response with the military-grade logistics of the UN Organization Stabilization Mission in the DRC (MONUSCO).
1. Strategic Air Bridge & Heavy Lift Architecture
Bypassing Insecure Overland Corridors: Deteriorated road infrastructure and militia ambushes render overland transport from Kinshasa or regional hubs non-viable for cold-chain biologics and urgent medical cargo. Under its Security Council Protection of Civilians (PoC) mandate, MONUSCO established a dedicated humanitarian air bridge linking Nairobi and Kinshasa directly to Bunia Airport.
Volume & Asset Integration: MONUSCO air assets have transported over 120 tons of emergency response cargo—including modular treatment tents, Tyvek PPE, laboratory reagents, and WASH kits—supplementing chartered flights from bilateral donors (such as U.S.-funded Samaritan’s Purse airlifts and Moroccan military medical donations).
2. Secure Operating Bases, Tactical Mobility, and UNPOL Integration
Hardened Logistics Hubs & Fleet Transfers: To protect WHO personnel following lethal attacks on health workers in eastern DRC, MONUSCO allocated dedicated, perimeter-secured office and warehousing facilities inside its Bunia logistics base. To sustain field mobility across 14+ affected health zones in Ituri, MONUSCO transferred armored personnel carriers, ambulances, 4x4 utility vehicles, and motorcycles directly to WHO field teams.

Community Sensitization & Police Support (UNPOL): Recognizing that coercive militarized enforcement triggers community resistance and drives cases underground, MONUSCO separates security from clinical care. Peacekeeping units conduct non-coercive public health outreach (using mobile loudspeakers in displaced camps in Tchabi and Fataki on hygiene, symptom recognition, and bushmeat risks), while UN Police (UNPOL) equip and train local Congolese National Police units in basic IPC protocols to secure treatment perimeters without impeding community access.
---------------
The United Nations Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF)—managed by the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) on behalf of the Emergency Relief Coordinator (ERC)—serves as the UN system's primary unearmarked, pooled liquidity mechanism. Operating with an annual funding target of $1 billion (with approximately $505.6 million mobilized and $495.7 million allocated across 2026 as of mid-November), CERF is specifically engineered to manage capital scarcity across simultaneous, competing global emergencies without requiring prolonged bilateral donor appeals.

To triage resources across sudden-onset shocks (such as the DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak and Gaza winter storms) and chronic, neglected emergencies (such as Afghanistan's winter crisis), CERF relies on a four-pillar architectural framework: dual allocation windows, quantitative composite indexing, pre-arranged parametric triggers, and complementary pooled-fund sequencing.

1. Dual-Window Architecture & Liquidity Allocation

CERF bifurcates its capital pool into two distinct operational windows to prevent acute, high-visibility emergencies from completely cannibalizing resources needed for protracted, media-neglected crises:

Includes fast-track grants for DRC health/logistics ($4M–$6.5M tranches) and Gaza common services.Hours to days. Agencies can start spending up to 6 weeks prior to formal disbursement via retroactive eligibility rules.Underfunded Emergencies (UFE) WindowInjects capital into chronically under-resourced operations twice annually (e.g., the $160M global UFE round across 12 crises, including $18M for Afghanistan's winter response).~28.5% of 2026 disbursements. Early-Warning Watchlist Integration: To avoid reactive bottlenecks during simultaneous shocks, the CERF Secretariat maintains a continuous global watchlist powered by OCHA's HDX Signals (integrating Armed Conflict Location & Event Data [ACLED], IPC food security projections, and automated Dataminr alerts). This allows the ERC to pre-position envelope ceilings before formal country-level proposals are finalized.
Thematic Envelopes & NGO Pass-Throughs: For systemic multi-country shocks (such as global food insecurity or the 2025 Cholera Early Action Framework), the ERC issues global thematic allocations. While CERF legally disburses only to UN agencies and IOM, OCHA has instituted fast-track pass-through modalities (such as a $25 million IOM-channeled envelope supporting 24 international and national NGOs across six countries) to bypass bureaucratic bottlenecks on the ground.
2. Quantitative Triage: The CERF Index for Risk and Vulnerability (CIRV)
When multiple protracted crises compete simultaneously for limited UFE funds, the CERF Secretariat eliminates political bias by ranking every crisis-affected country (0 to 100 scale) using the CERF Index for Risk and Vulnerability (CIRV):
Equal-Weighted Composite Structure: For countries with active crises, CIRV aggregates three equally weighted (1/3 each) quantitative pillars:
INFORM Risk Index: Evaluates structural hazards, exposure, socio-economic vulnerability, and institutional lack of coping capacity across 50+ indicators (3–5 year horizon).
INFORM Severity Index: Measures the immediate physical and human impact of active crises across 30 indicators, including displacement scale and operational access complexity.
Dynamic Shock & Early-Warning Composite: Integrates real-time Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC Phases 3–5) data, ACLED conflict intensity metrics (deadliness, civilian danger, armed group fragmentation), and Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) early-warning alerts.
Scatterplot Gap Analysis: CERF cross-plots each country's CIRV severity score against real-time donor coverage ratios tracked via OCHA's Financial Tracking Service (FTS). Countries falling into the high-CIRV / lowest-FTS-coverage quadrant are shortlisted for UFE allocations, followed by technical consultations with the Underfunded Emergencies Working Group (UFEWG) and NGO consortia (ICVA) to verify absorptive capacity.
3. Parametric Anticipatory Action (AA) & Climate Financing
To prevent predictable climate hazards from compounding active conflict emergencies, CERF has ring-fenced over $100 million across more than 20 countries in pre-arranged Anticipatory Action (AA) frameworks, bolstered by the dedicated CERF Climate Action Account.
Automated Parametric Triggers: Rather than waiting for post-disaster damage assessments, AA frameworks bind scientific forecasting thresholds (e.g., Standardized Precipitation Index [SPI] drought probabilities or Indian Ocean Dipole anomalies) to pre-agreed multi-sectoral action plans.
Sub-Minute Disbursement: Once a meteorological or epidemiological trigger threshold is breached (such as Kenya's 2026 drought framework releasing up to $5 million upon hitting a 40%–60% severe drought probability threshold), pre-committed CERF financing is automatically unlocked—in as little as one minute—allowing agencies to distribute cash transfers, climate-resilient seeds, and WASH supplies before peak displacement occurs.
4. Dual-Track Complementarity with Country-Based Pooled Funds (CBPFs)
Because CERF operates globally at the macro-UN agency level, OCHA pairs it with Country-Based Pooled Funds (CBPFs) (which allocated $893 million across 23 contexts alongside CERF's $312 million in the 2025 full-year cycle) to create a two-tier liquidity engine:
Temporal & Operational Sequencing: In high-intensity multi-crisis theaters (such as Occupied Palestinian Territory, Sudan, DRC, and Afghanistan), the Humanitarian Coordinator (HC) deploys CERF to finance immediate, capital-intensive UN agency common services—such as WFP logistics clusters, UNHAS air bridges, and bulk medical procurement—while simultaneously mobilizing CBPF grants directly to local and national NGOs for last-mile community distribution.
Synchronized Co-Financing: In compound emergencies (such as Afghanistan's synchronized drought and winter response), CERF and CBPFs operate under unified trigger frameworks, co-financing complementary sectoral packages so international supply chains and local responders activate concurrently.

$SPY MARKET UPDATE: TARGETS HIT. NOW WHAT? 🎯

Last week’s bearish roadmap played out perfectly.

I called for the $735 gap fill and a potential 200-day SMA retest around $729–726. Both targets were hit, with SPY making a fresh low near $727.

The bearish 10/100 and 20/100-day SMA crossovers, repeated resistance rejections and weakening momentum warned of another leg lower.

All downside targets achieved. My final put is closed, profits secured, and I’m entirely in cash. No more shorts for now.

So, what’s next?

1. Has SPY bottomed? Not necessarily.

Hitting downside targets doesn’t automatically end a correction.

SPY remains below its major short and intermediate term moving averages, with both the 10 and 20-day SMAs below the 100-day SMA.

Those bearish crosses helped confirm the decline. For a convincing reversal, I’d eventually want the opposite: both averages reclaiming the 100-day SMA.

I don’t need to wait for that to trade a bounce, but a tradable relief rally isn’t necessarily a confirmed bottom.

2. Preferred long entry zone: $721-715

Ideally, SPY retests its 50-week SMA around $720–721, with additional liquidity support near $715–716.

That $715–721 zone offers attractive potential risk/reward for calls, provided buyers defend it.

Could it mark the bottom before another rally towards ATHs? Absolutely. But I’d want confirmation rather than blindly calling a bottom in a falling market to sound cool.

3. What if SPY rallies immediately?

First resistance is $741, an area that has repeatedly rejected price.

Above that, $750–751 is the next major test.

A rejection around $751 could offer another short opportunity, especially below declining moving averages.

Conversely, reclaiming $751 and the 5 and 10-day SMAs would be an encouraging first step.

A sustained reclaim of the 100-day SMA, with a bullish 10/100 and 20/100 crossovers, would strengthen the case for a genuine reversal and potentially new ATHs.

One reclaim doesn’t confirm a bottom. Improving price structure, momentum and moving averages together carry more weight.

4. Nvidia earnings is why I’m cautious

Nvidia delivered another widely anticipated earnings beat. My bigger concern was guidance and confidence surrounding the leadership transition.

The board ruled out Jensen Huang’s immediate return, but longer-term leadership uncertainty remains.

I listened to the earnings call and didn’t find the reassurance particularly convincing.

Nvidia initially jumped several percentage points, pulling the broader market higher, but those gains have already started fading.

I flagged the rally to subscribers as suspicious. Strong results don’t guarantee sustained upside when expectations are elevated and the broader technical structure remains weak.

Let’s see whether buyers defend the gains during regular trading.

5. Anthropic IPO is potential liquidity catalyst

Thursday’s anticipated Anthropic IPO introduces another variable.

Could investors raise cash ahead of the offering, pressuring other tech stocks? Possibly.

Could it instead lift AI sector sentiment? Also possible.

I won’t assume either outcome. Price action will determine my next move.

6. Why I’m staying in cash

With VIX recently above 25, calls face potential implied-volatility contraction. SPY could bounce while falling IV still pressures options premiums.

That’s partly why I didn’t immediately switch from puts to calls after hitting my targets.

I’d rather wait for a cleaner entry: a confirmed reaction around $720–715 or improving bullish structure higher up.

BOTTOM LINE

My bearish targets are complete, puts closed and profits secured. Now I’m preparing for the next opportunity.

I’m not automatically bullish because the market fell, nor permanently bearish after successfully trading the decline.

Upside resistance: $741–742, then $750–751.

Preferred deeper dip buying zone: $720–715.

A convincing reversal could offer calls. Another rejection could offer puts. I’ll adapt.

text:
1 AM Top-of-the-Hour News

The associated press has called the Alaska Senate race in favor of Democrat Mary Peltola over two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.: “Thank you, Alaska. We did it. From ADA to Metlakatla to Ukavik, you have made your voices heard, and it's clear that the status quo in DC cannot go on any longer. ”
It was the last Senate race that was left to be decided.
The victory gives Democrats their ninth Senate flip in the midterms. It's the most for the party since 1958.

Democrat Chuck Schumer says he will head the Senate when the new term begins in January.: “I'm confident I'll be the next leader, I have the votes, and we're all going to roll up our sleeves and we're going to focus on lowering costs, ending corruption. ”
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen says he is also running to be majority leader - saying the sweeping victory by Democrats in the midterm elections was a mandate from voters for change.

President Trump is in Manila holding bilateral talks with Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
The president said that the United States is expanding its defense cooperation with Manila, and will probably do "something big" on nuclear power.: “With this visit, we're building on these ties to make our partnership even closer, although I don't imagine it can get much closer because of the relationship that we've had for a long time. ”
Philippine president Marcos:: “We are also exploring new areas of cooperation, particularly in technology, where American leadership and innovation continues to lead the way. We also see tremendous opportunities to work more closely through American leadership and super intelligence. ”
The president is next headed to China for an historical three way meeting with Xi Xinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.

The National Security Agency's highly classified communications system went down on Tuesday.
The outage impacted the N-S-A Net, which is responsible for sending and receiving top secret information.
NewsNation's Hannah Brandt reports: “A spokesperson says this was temporary. It happened during scheduled routine maintenance, they say, and they say, quote, mission critical capabilities remain fully operational. But this incident only adds to the growing list of technical disruptions that US companies and different systems that we've seen, adding to the concern over it as well. ”
Reports say it does not appear to be a cyber attack.
Apple also reported full outages with its Apple Music, App Store and AppleCare services, with issues on its iCloud interface. The company blamed an internal update for the problems.
Marriot International reported their own technology problems on Tuesday.

Nvidia has rejected former CEO Jensen Huang's offer to return to the company. The decision was made despite pressure from Silicon Valley and president Trump to reinstate Huang as CEO. Huang resigned after his admission to extramarital affairs, including with a Chinese businesswoman U.S. intelligence suspects could be a Chinese spy.

“I'm Spencer Raine. Senate Majority Leader John Thune says Republicans are taking a look at Secretary Sean Duffy's request for fixing the nation's air traffic control system. He says Safe Skies is a bipartisan priority, but he's not quite ready to reach for the checkbook. $50 billion is a number that obviously they, as they work through and try to explain how that would be utilized, there were some very good questions asked by our members, and I think the The number that they originally came out with is one that reflects not just the immediate needs when it comes to modernizing our air traffic control system and doing some upgrades at the towers. At the same time, he suggested some part of this money may need to come from the appropriations process. He says his party is planning a way to get some Democrat buy-in, but they're also considering a way to get a measure passed with just Republican support. Spencer Rain, Worldwide News Network. ”

An internal network that the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information went offline after what one U-S official described as “routine maintenance.” A defense official said Tuesday that the problem affected NSANet, a classified internal network used by employees of the agency.  Larry Magid, CEO of the Internet Safety Organization, Connect Safely:: “This recent NSA outage is on top of numerous other outages over the last week, starting with Microsoft Outlook, which disrupted email around the world, the FAA outage from Friday that grounded most flights in the US, a United Airlines outage, a number of banks that lost access to some online services, and even Apple's iCloud sign-in failures. ”
NSA Net is used for internally communicating classified and sensitive information. The report says there's no evidence that the issue stems from a cyber attack.

text:
Prosecutors Say C-130 Worth About $60 Million Was Damaged at Shannon Airport

A grand jury in New York indicted Daithi O’Corrain, 48, in connection with damage to a US military C-130 at Shannon Airport in Ireland. The aircraft, a C-130 Hercules, is estimated to be worth approximately $60 million, giving the alleged damage a substantial stated value even though the facts do not specify a repair bill. Prosecutors accuse O’Corrain of damaging the plane, and the indictment concerns destruction of government property; the accusation is not a finding of guilt. If convicted of that offense, he could receive a prison sentence of up to 10 years. The stated value describes the aircraft, while the possible prison term describes the consequence attached to a conviction, so the two figures measure different things.

The prosecution account begins with an alleged breach of the airport’s security boundary on 11 April. Prosecutors say O’Corrain then entered the parked C-130 and shut himself inside by barricading it. The aircraft was not described as flying at the time; it was parked at Shannon when the alleged actions took place. According to prosecutors, he cut wiring and hydraulic lines, broke the cockpit’s gauges, and struck the aircraft’s outer surface with an axe. They also allege that he put ball bearings into the plane’s fuel tanks, adding a separate form of interference to the damage described inside and outside the aircraft.

The indictment also describes how the plane’s windows were covered: O’Corrain allegedly used hammocks belonging to the crew for that purpose. The cockpit windshield, however, was left uncovered, according to the indictment. This detail records the alleged arrangement inside the aircraft, rather than adding a separate estimate of damage or a further charge. The other alleged actions cover several parts of the C-130: its cockpit instruments, wiring, hydraulic lines, exterior and fuel tanks. The account therefore identifies multiple kinds of alleged damage, but it supplies no itemized monetary total for them.

The plane belonged to the US Air National Guard, and it was traveling toward a military assignment in another country. The aircraft was rendered inoperable, according to the account of its intended journey and the incident. That means the reported consequence was not limited to damage to a parked aircraft: the C-130 could no longer continue to its military task. The available facts do not identify the country, the assignment’s purpose, or how long the aircraft remained out of service. They also do not provide a count of personnel or other aircraft affected, so the stated operational impact is specific to this C-130 and its planned journey.

The case has legal tracks in both the United States and Ireland, according to the reported charges and arrest. An Garda Síochána arrested O’Corrain immediately after the attack, and Irish authorities charged him with criminal damage and trespassing. Separately, a grand jury in New York indicted him over the alleged damage to US government property. The possible 10-year prison term belongs to the US destruction-of-government-property charge and applies only if there is a conviction. The facts identify the Irish charges but do not give a possible sentence for them, so that penalty should not be confused with the stated US maximum.

Manhattan US attorney Jamie McDonald said the indictment was intended to make clear that attacks on US military property would not be accepted. His statement sets out the prosecutor’s position on the alleged conduct; it does not establish that O’Corrain committed the offense. James Barnacle, who leads the FBI’s New York office, characterized the act as more than unplanned vandalism. That description is Barnacle’s assessment, while the sequence of alleged entry and damage is presented in the prosecutors’ account. Neither official statement changes the status of the claims as allegations in an indictment.

Supporters organized an online fundraiser and said O’Corrain had acted in protest against the US-Israel war in Gaza and US backing for Israel’s genocide. That account is attributed to the fundraiser’s supporters, rather than presented as a finding by the grand jury or prosecutors. The facts do not establish that the stated political motive was O’Corrain’s motive, and they do not describe him making that claim himself. The fundraiser’s explanation therefore sits alongside, but is distinct from, the legal account of the alleged breach and damage.

The reported aircraft value of approximately $60 million is a description of the C-130’s worth, not a quantified estimate of the harm caused in this incident. No cost for repairs, replacement, or lost use is supplied, although the aircraft was said to have become inoperable. Likewise, the possible sentence of up to 10 years is a maximum identified for a conviction, not a report of a sentence imposed. These distinctions matter because the aircraft’s valuation, its operational status, and the potential legal penalty describe separate consequences of the case. The available account does not state the outcome of the indictment or the Irish proceedings.

Taken together, the allegations concern entry into a secured airport area, actions inside a parked military aircraft, and damage that left it unable to operate. The plane’s role in a military assignment abroad gives the reported loss of operability a stated operational context beyond its approximate $60 million value. The indictment, the Irish charges, and the officials’ remarks describe the legal response and the authorities’ view of the incident, while leaving guilt unresolved. The supporters’ stated protest rationale offers a different account of motive, but the facts establish only that supporters circulated it through a fundraiser. What is specified is the alleged sequence, the aircraft’s stated value and assignment, the charges, and the maximum US prison term if conviction follows.

text:
Dfense Head Roundup 🏭🇺🇸🧵

1/ General Flash raised $128 million across seed and Series A to scale U.S. critical-metals output. Lux Capital, Construct Capital, and Overmatch Ventures led. The Cambridge, Massachusetts firm runs a 20-ton-per-year pilot near MIT and aims for 1,000 metric tons a year in 2027.
 Broke 8:55 a.m. ET. It's a U.S. source of tungsten, titanium, and tantalum, coming just ahead of the Jan. 1 rules that start cutting Chinese supply out of defense supply chains. The $128M covers both rounds combined, the 1,000-ton figure is a target, and no buyer has signed yet.
2/ Genesis AI raised a $500 million Series A led by @khoslaventures, Premji Invest, and Eclipse. The firm is building dexterous humanoid robots trained with force data from sensor gloves. It has built 30 to 40 Enos units. A U.S. contractor is slated to start next year.
 Broke 9:00 a.m. ET. It's a huge humanoid round with a plan to manufacture in the U.S. No valuation was disclosed, and the hands still wear out after a few weeks of regular work.

3/ @QuaiseEnergy signed a power-purchase deal with @Google for 50 MW of superhot geothermal power from Project Obsidian in Central Oregon. Deliveries may start as early as 2030 for Google data centers in The Dalles and the region. The first phase will use conventional drilling.
 Broke 6:50 a.m. ET. It's the first time a hyperscaler has agreed to buy superhot geothermal power. No contract value was disclosed, so ignore the $500M figure some recaps are using. Quaise's millimeter-wave drilling isn't part of phase 1.
4/ Giga Energy signed a 10-year, $1 billion lease with an undisclosed U.S. AI cloud provider for Project Clay, a 60 MW data center in Hunt County, Texas. The campus is targeted for service in spring 2027. Giga says the site will use no water for compute.
 Broke 11:35 a.m. ET. A mid-size, factory-built AI campus makes a good contrast with yesterday's Blackstone/AWS deal. The $1B is the value of the lease over 10 years, not a sale price.

5/ EQT agreed to buy Flatiron Energy from Hull Street Energy. Flatiron builds utility-scale batteries in the eastern U.S. It cites a 24 GWh portfolio, 6 GWh under long-term contracts, and 2 GWh under construction. The price was not disclosed. Close is targeted for Q4 2026.
 Broke about 9:30 a.m. ET. Grid congestion and data-center demand are pushing up the value of East Coast batteries. The 24 GWh is mostly pipeline, not operating capacity.
6/ AMPERA agreed to combine with Berto Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: TACO) at about $900 million pre-money. Up to $357 million in gross proceeds assumes no trust redemptions. AMPERA is developing factory-built power units and a planned 15 MW thorium reactor. The deal is not closed.
 Broke 6:55 p.m. ET. It's a Florida-linked company (Palm Beach Gardens) using a SPAC to go public with a thorium reactor. Any near-term revenue would come from heat-recovery units, not the reactor, which is still just a design.

7/ Trinity Capital committed $100 million in debt to Phononic, a North Carolina firm that makes solid-state thermoelectric cooling systems for AI data centers. The funds are meant to expand manufacturing. The $100 million is a commitment, not a stated cash draw today.
 Broke 8:00 a.m. ET. Heat is the limit for AI chips, and this money is for building more U.S. cooling hardware.
8/ @Argentum_AI and @Kyndryl signed a 20-year, $630 million collaboration for an initial 10 MW at Kyndryl's Boulder, Colorado site. Argentum will deploy NVIDIA B300 systems. Deployment is underway. The $630 million is the stated long-term contract value, not a sale of the site.
 Broke 12:00 p.m. ET. It's AI capacity added to an existing enterprise data center instead of a new gigawatt campus.

9/ @BostonDynamics and @GlobalFoundries will expand Spot robot inspections across GF fabs in Malta, New York; Burlington, Vermont; Dresden; and Singapore. GF will also be the first semiconductor maker to test the Atlas humanoid, with on-site trials slated to start in early 2027.
 Broke 9:00 a.m. ET. It's a humanoid on a chip-fab floor for the first time, and a nice follow-up to yesterday's Malta groundbreaking. Atlas is only being evaluated, not put into production.

Sources: General Flash, Genesis AI, Quaise/Google, Giga Energy, EQT/Flatiron, AMPERA, Phononic, Argentum/Kyndryl, Boston Dynamics/GF

“SpaceX was allowed to build in Boca Chica through a mix of strategic location shopping, intense state political backing, and an incremental permitting process that started small and scaled up after billions were already poured in concrete.

1. The "Bait-and-Switch" Permitting Path
•Starting Small (2012–2014): When SpaceX applied for federal approval, it pitched Boca Chica as a quiet commercial spaceport for up to 12 launches a year of its much smaller Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets—not the massive, experimental Starship system.

•Passing the Initial Review: Based on those smaller numbers, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a full Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) in 2014 concluding the site would have minimal impact on neighboring South Padre Island and Port Isabel (about 5 miles away).

•Scaling Up Once Built: After building its factories and launch pad, SpaceX pivoted to Starship—a rocket roughly twice as powerful as the Saturn V moon rocket—and repeatedly asked the FAA for amended approvals (such as the 2022 Programmatic Environmental Assessment) rather than starting over from scratch.

2. Aggressive Texas State & Local Support
•Changing State Law (2013): Before SpaceX even broke ground, the Texas Legislature passed a law specifically allowing Cameron County to close Boca Chica Beach and Highway 4 for spaceflight activities—something previously illegal under Texas’s strict Open Beaches Act.

•Millions in Incentives: Texas state officials and local economic development boards offered SpaceX roughly $15 million to $20 million in direct grants, tax abatements, and infrastructure funding to beat out competing bids from Florida, Georgia, and Puerto Rico.

•Economic Desperation: Cameron County has long been one of the poorest counties in the U.S. Local officials viewed SpaceX as a once-in-a-generation economic lifeline and largely waved through early land purchases and zoning requests.

3. Exploiting a Regulatory Gray Area

•Fragmented Land Ownership: Unlike Cape Canaveral—where the federal government owns a massive, unified 15,000-acre buffer zone—Boca Chica was a patchwork of tiny private lots, state parkland, and federal wildlife refuges. SpaceX quietly bought up dozens of small residential lots in Boca Chica Village through shell companies (like Dogleg Park LLC) before announcing its plans, establishing a foothold right in the middle of PROTECTED STATE and FEDERAL land.

•No Zoning Laws: Unincorporated Cameron County had almost no traditional zoning restrictions preventing heavy industrial rocket manufacturing next to a coastal village or WILDLIFE REFUGE.

4. Strategic Leverage Over Federal Regulators

Once SpaceX became NASA’s sole contractor to land astronauts on the Moon (via the Artemis program) and the Pentagon's primary launch provider, federal agencies faced enormous political pressure not to slow down Starship development—leading regulators to repeatedly grant conditional approvals and mitigations rather than shutting the site down.”  -Google Ai

Hyperscale (the big cloud platforms) did $60.1B, up 23% QoQ, and took about 61% of the $18.6B sequential Data Center gain. In August the hyperscale reacceleration was promised for Q4. It showed up in Q3. ACIE (AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise: neoclouds, sovereigns, corporates) did $47.5B, nearly triple a year ago.

3. Fiscal 2028 got raised, on a bigger base. The growth outlook moves to about 75% from 70%, and that now compounds on a base made larger by a $7.8B Q3 beat. Management's case for confidence is demand plus secured supply. Export controls are not in the number yet and are still being studied. No figure was given for what demand would look like if supply weren't the limit.

4. Q4 is the margin floor, by their own word. Gross margin is guided to 71% to 72%, down from 74.9%, after holding near 75% for three straight quarters. Q4 is called the bottom because it fills purchase orders already on the books. My read is that those orders were priced before memory costs climbed. Fiscal 2028 stays at 72% to 73%. Long-term pricing power against custom chips (ASICs) got no answer and was deferred to the future. 

5. Nvidia is now guaranteeing its customers' buildouts. Total guarantees rose to $118B from $108.5B. $105B of that is credit support for SB Energy's 4.25 GW Ohio campus, which will host Nvidia infrastructure for OpenAI on a 20-year lease. Total commitments, including leases and equity stakes, reached $518B, up from $366B a quarter ago. The CFO commentary itself says neoclouds (GPU-rental clouds like CoreWeave and Nebius) and frontier labs are growing faster than their balance sheets can support. The defense is that a guarantee only starts once a building is ready, with the first expected in fiscal 2029. On whether the commitment language changed: "Is it new? No. Did we change anything? No."

6. Supply goes to customers who can build, not to whoever bids highest. Capacity goes first to buyers with land, power and shell (the site, the grid hookup, the building) plus capital and offtake already lined up, and everyone pays the same price. Suppliers come first for Nvidia's own capital, ahead of customer financing. $28.1B went back to shareholders in Q3, with $227B of buyback authorization left.

Bottom line: The operating numbers are as strong as they have ever been: 103% growth, the fastest ramp in company history and a raised fiscal 2028. The stock went into the print down about 36% from its October 6 high and rose only about 4% after hours on a $7.8B beat. So the market isn't questioning the demand. It's pricing who leads the company.

STATEHOUSE PRESS RELEASE

PRESIDENT TINUBU APPROVES KEBBI INLAND DRY PORT, AS FORMER GOVERNORS OF THE STATE BACK HIS RE-ELECTION

* PRESIDENT TINUBU PROMISES COMPLETION OF LANDMARK PROJECTS AND IMPROVED SECURITY

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Tuesday approved the full operationalisation of the Tsamiya Inland Dry Port in Kebbi, describing the facility as strategic towards boosting the state's economy.
He also thanked the people of the state for their massive turnout and warm reception during the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally at the Haliru Abdu Multi Purpose Stadium in Birnin Kebbi. President Tinubu said he would not take their support and confidence for granted.
One of the campaign's highlights was former governors declaring they would work for President Tinubu’s re-election because he supported the state in times of need.
The former governors are Sen. Adamu Aleiro,  Sai'du Usman Nasamu Dankingari and Minister of Budget and Economic Planning Sen. Atiku Bagudu.
The President reaffirmed his administration's commitment to complete ongoing landmark infrastructure projects, especially the Illela-Badagry Superhighway, which passes through Kebbi, as well as other federal road networks within Kebbi State.
He commended Kebbi State Governor Comrade Dr Nasir Idris for complementing the federal government's road-construction efforts and promised to expand the state's agricultural programmes.
"We will expand the existing agricultural programmes. We will support rice mills in Birnin Kebbi, Argungu, Bagudo and Yauri.
" We will ensure that the Zuru–Rijau Road is actualised, while the Koko–Dabai road will soon be completed through the Kebbi State Government platform. We will rehabilitate the Goronyo–Argungu irrigation scheme and the Zauro Polder Project so that your farmers can farm year-round," the President said.
On Security, President Tinubu pledged to strengthen further the national security architecture and support sub-nationals' capacity to fight crime by signing the state police bill into law.
"We are mindful of the challenges in Zuru, Danko/Wasagu, Sakaba, Bagudo, Arewa, Shanga and some parts of Maiyama. We shall work together to end insecurity.
" In the meantime, we have deployed more troops to the state. We have provided more equipment to the military and police. We have approved new operating bases in Zuru, Bagudo and Yauri.
" By the grace of God, the days of bandits terrorising our innocent farmers are numbered, as we step up efforts to ensure that no farmer in Kebbi will be afraid to go to his farm again", the President assured.
He further stated his administration's determination to ensure peaceful elections while thanking APC leadership, supporters, and residents of Birnin Kebbi for their solidarity and impressive turnout.
In his remarks, Vice President Kashim Shettima reminded the audience of the support President Tinubu gave to late former President Muhammadu Buhari, enabling him to consolidate and win the 2015 presidential election. He urged the northern voters to reciprocate the gesture.
The Vice President told the gathering that President Tinubu sacrificed his resources and comfort to give the North what it wished in 2015. He also thanked the North for giving the President 60.2% of the votes that gave the APC victory in 2023.
"The North repaid that kindness, and we are even more grateful that you are prepared to do the same in the coming election in January because you have rejected the lies, the distortions, the half-truths.
Earlier, the host Governor, Nasir Idris, commended the President for graciously approving his request to fully operationalise the Kebbi Inland Dry Port and other critical road projects in the state.
Governor Idris assured the President of their support towards his re-election bid as a mark of appreciation for his support for the state's socio-economic development.
The APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, commended some guests' testimonies on President Tinubu's commitment to infrastructure development in the country, especially in education, health, and security.
He assured the President that the North has resolved to support his re-election in 2027.
Sen. AbdulAziz Yari, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), thanked Kebbi residents for the massive turnout and commended the President for his massive investment in the state's economy.
Yari urged Kebbi residents to come out en masse and vote for the President in the forthcoming 2027 Presidential general elections.
He said the creation of the Federal Ministry of Livestock Development was deliberate, aimed at addressing farmer-herder clashes in the north and supporting the ongoing construction of the Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, designed to ease traffic along the corridor in line with the vision of Nigeria's founding fathers.
Yari urged voters to disregard the deceitful voices of the opposition parties.
The Kebbi APC Presidential campaign rally was attended by First Lady Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, Governors Uba Sani of Kaduna, Dauda Lawal of Zamfara, Mai Mala Buni of Yobe, Babagana Zulum of Borno and Ahmad Aliyu of Sokoto.
Others include Speaker of the House of Representatives Tajudeen Abbas; Senators Adams Oshiomhole and Ali Modu Sheriff; Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning Doris Uzoka-Anite; Minister of Housing Muttaqha Darma; and former governors Ahmed Yerima of Zamfara, Ibrahim Shema of Katsina, and Abdullahi Ganduje.
The APC Campaign train has continued to criss-cross the country, engaging party stakeholders and Nigerians across the six geopolitical zones.
Bayo Onanuga
Special Adviser to the President
(Information & Strategy)

text:
Brad Pitt bought his elderly neighbor’s house — then reportedly let him continue living there rent-free for the rest of his life. ❤️

The unusual arrangement came to light through actress Cassandra Peterson, better known as Elvira, who once owned the Los Feliz property that became the center of Pitt’s sprawling Los Angeles estate.

Over the years, Pitt purchased several neighboring properties to expand the compound. One belonged to an elderly widower named John, who was around 90 at the time.

Rather than require John to leave his longtime home after purchasing it, Pitt reportedly made him an offer:

Stay as long as you live. No rent required.

It turned into a considerably longer commitment than anyone may have expected.

John lived to 105 years old, meaning the arrangement appears to have lasted roughly 15 years. Peterson later joked that John “just kept living forever,” adding that Pitt was probably thinking, “Well, you know, he can live there till he dies, which might be any minute now.”

But John kept going.

An important distinction often lost when the story is retold is that Pitt was already buying surrounding properties for his estate. The generous part wasn’t simply purchasing John’s house — it was allowing an elderly man to remain in his home afterward without paying rent.

Peterson also remembered Pitt as consistently kind and respectful during the years they were neighbors.

For John, a property sale therefore didn't mean losing the place he had called home.

He sold his house at around 90 — and was reportedly allowed to keep calling it home until 105. ❤️

Would you make the same arrangement if you bought a home from someone who had lived there for decades?

Sources: Cassandra Peterson’s People interview; Fox News; NZ Herald; Tribune India; La Vanguardia.

text:
ALIKO DANGOTE ARRIVES IN UGANDA FOR HIGH-LEVEL TALKS ON OIL REFINERY AND INDUSTRIAL INVESTMENTS.

By Keefa Nuwahereza.
Africa’s richest man, Nigerian industrialist Aliko Dangote, arrived in Uganda in mid-November 2026 and was received by Hon. Hajjat Aminah Mukalazi, the Minister of State for Finance, Planning and Economic Development responsible for Privatisation and Investment. The visit, which sets the stage for a high-level engagement with President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni at State House Entebbe, follows intensive discussions held days earlier in Nigeria and signals Uganda’s determined push to attract large-scale African capital into its petroleum and mineral value-addition agenda.

The arrival comes less than a week after a Ugandan government delegation toured the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals complex and the Dangote Fertiliser Limited plants in Lekki, Lagos, on 14 November 2026. Led by Dr. Monica Musenero Masanza, Minister of Energy and Mineral Development, and accompanied by Hajjat Amina Mukalazi, the team presented concrete investment proposals focused on transforming Uganda’s natural resources into finished products within the country rather than exporting them in raw form.

At the centre of the pitch is Uganda’s long-planned 60,000-barrel-per-day oil refinery in the Hoima area of western Uganda, near the Lake Albert oil fields. Officials invited the Dangote Group to take a leading role in developing the facility, citing the conglomerate’s proven capacity to finance, engineer, construct and operate world-scale industrial plants. Mukalazi described the refinery as a major national industrial priority, noting that a Ugandan plant could serve inland East African markets and complement the large refinery Dangote is developing in Lamu, Kenya, which is oriented toward coastal and maritime demand. She told the Nigerian industrialist that estimates presented by the delegation would require technical assessment by his team, but expressed confidence that the partnership could move forward with strong political support from Kampala.

Beyond refining, the proposals encompass fertiliser blending and phosphate processing, as well as salt production. Uganda possesses phosphate deposits and salt resources that could support domestic manufacturing of fertilisers and industrial chemicals. The ministers argued that these ventures could share infrastructure, logistics and distribution networks with the refinery, creating an integrated industrial complex. “Our crude, our phosphate, our salt are waiting to be turned into fuel, fertilisers and chemicals here in Africa and in Uganda by Africans,” Mukalazi stated during the Lagos meetings. She emphasised that the investments would generate jobs, enable skills transfer, create opportunities for local businesses and reduce the country’s heavy reliance on imported petroleum products and agricultural inputs.

The timing of Dangote’s visit aligns with Uganda’s broader industrialisation strategy under President Museveni, who has long insisted that oil production must be accompanied by domestic refining. Museveni has previously stated that crude oil should not leave the ground without a refinery in place, reflecting a policy preference for value addition over pure raw-material exports. While Uganda has advanced the East African Crude Oil Pipeline toward Tanzania and signed an earlier agreement with UAE-based Alpha MBM Investments for the Hoima refinery (with Uganda National Oil Company holding a 40 percent stake), progress toward a final investment decision has faced delays. Courting Dangote offers an alternative or complementary pathway rooted in African private-sector capacity and experience.

Dangote’s track record makes him a natural partner for such ambitions. His group operates Africa’s largest single-train refinery in Nigeria, a project that has demonstrated the feasibility of building and running complex petroleum and petrochemical facilities on the continent. The conglomerate is pursuing a Vision 2030 expansion plan that includes significant investments across Africa, and executives have indicated that East African opportunities fit within that strategy. During the Lagos visit, senior Dangote officials, including Group Vice President Devakumar Edwin and others, received the Ugandan team and heard the case for partnership.

For Uganda, successful engagement could accelerate local content development, create thousands of construction and operational jobs, and strengthen regional value chains within the East African Community. It would also reinforce the narrative of African-led industrialisation, with technology, capital and management expertise flowing between Nigerian and Ugandan institutions rather than depending solely on external partners. Government officials have pledged to address regulatory bottlenecks and provide an enabling environment, building on Mukalazi’s dual roles in investment promotion and local-content advocacy.

As Dangote’s delegation prepares for the State House meeting, the discussions are expected to move from the exploratory phase initiated in Lagos toward more detailed technical, commercial and financing talks. No binding agreement has yet been announced, and any commitment will depend on rigorous feasibility assessments. Nevertheless, the visit itself marks a notable step in Uganda’s efforts to convert its petroleum and mineral endowment into sustained industrial growth and economic diversification.

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. (RMS)

News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

text:
🇨🇳 Who Will Shape the Next Phase of Globalisation?

Xi Jinping’s address at the opening of the 2026 APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on 18 November was about considerably more than trade, investment or regional cooperation. It was a carefully constructed statement of China’s ambition to shape the next phase of the international economic order.

Emphasising peace, openness, technological innovation and multilateral cooperation, Xi presented China as a defender of globalisation at a time when protectionism, geopolitical rivalry and economic fragmentation are challenging the foundations of international trade. Without directly confronting Washington, his message offered an implicit contrast between China’s declared commitment to economic integration and America’s increasingly transactional approach to international economic relations.

But Beijing’s proposition goes beyond rhetoric. By promising greater market access, regulatory reforms and opportunities in manufacturing, services and emerging technologies, Xi is seeking to reassure international businesses that China remains an indispensable economic partner. At the same time, his call for a more multipolar international order reflects a broader ambition to give China and other emerging economies greater influence over global governance.

There is, however, a distinction between advocating openness and practising it. China’s willingness to reform its domestic regulatory environment, provide reciprocal market access and address concerns about competitive conditions will ultimately determine the credibility of its message.

The underlying ambition is nevertheless unmistakable. Beijing is not necessarily seeking to dismantle globalisation, but to acquire a greater role in defining its rules, institutions and future direction. The question is therefore no longer simply whether China intends to participate in the existing international order, but how much influence it will exercise in shaping what comes next.

The contest is not just about who trades with whom. It is increasingly about who writes the rules of the global economy.
